distractors.reason: We don't say 'much tired'. 'Much' is not used before an adjective like 'tired'; we use it with verbs (I like it much) or comparatives (much better).
'Strong' is an adjective, not an adverb. We say 'strong tea', but we don't say 'strong tired'.
'Big' is an adjective. The word before 'tired' must be an adverb that shows how tired someone is.

example_sentence: My mother is ___ tired after work.
l1_interference: Українці часто плутають 'very' і 'much', бо обидва слова перекладаються як 'дуже'. Перед прикметником у англійській завжди кажуть 'very tired', а не 'much tired'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the most common adverb before an adjective when we want to make it stronger: very tired, very big, very happy.

related_collocations.example: My grandmother's kitchen is always very clean.
The whole family was very happy.

memory_tip: VERY + adjective (very tired, very big) | MUCH + verb or comparative (I like it much, much better)
